question: What is another commonly used term for nosocomial infections?
explanation: Nosocomial infections are officially referred to as healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) because they are acquired while receiving treatment in a healthcare facility. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why are hospitalized patients particularly susceptible to nosocomial infections?

options.A: They consume a high-fiber hospital diet
options.B: They are frequently immunocompromised and undergo invasive procedures
options.C: They spend too much time outdoors walking around hospital grounds
options.D: They lack access to modern electronic devices

explanation: Hospitalized patients are often immunocompromised and subjected to invasive procedures, making them much more vulnerable to acquiring infections. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h1)

question: How many total links make up the standard chain of infection model?
explanation: The chain of infection consists of six distinct links: infectious agent, reservoir, portal of exit, mode of transmission, portal of entry, and susceptible host. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which link in the chain of infection is directly interrupted when a nurse performs proper hand hygiene?
explanation: Hand hygiene removes pathogens from the hands, thereby breaking the mode of transmission between patients and surfaces. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h2)

question: To which group of patients should standard precautions be applied?

options.B: Only patients with visible blood on their skin
options.C: All patients regardless of their diagnosis or infection status
options.D: Only patients admitted to surgical wards

explanation: Standard precautions must be applied universally to all patients in the healthcare setting, regardless of their diagnosis or presumed infection status. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which bodily excretion is specifically excluded from standard precautions fluids?
explanation: Standard precautions apply to all body fluids except sweat, regardless of whether it contains visible blood. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which type of precaution requires the use of an Airborne Infection Isolation Room (AIIR) with negative pressure?
explanation: Airborne precautions require negative pressure rooms to prevent infectious particles from escaping into the surrounding corridor and facility air. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h4)

question: What personal protective equipment is specifically emphasized for healthcare workers providing care under droplet precautions?
explanation: Droplet precautions require wearing a standard surgical mask when working within close proximity to the patient to block large respiratory droplets. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h4)

question: According to the WHO, what is the minimum duration for performing hand washing with soap and water?
explanation: Hand washing with soap and water must last at least 40 to 60 seconds to ensure adequate removal of microorganisms from all skin surfaces. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h5)

question: When is it mandatory to use soap and water instead of an alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: Before taking a patient's vital signs
options.B: When hands are visibly soiled with blood or body fluids
options.C: Immediately before entering the hospital ward
options.D: After charting on an electronic medical record

explanation: Soap and water must be used when hands are visibly dirty or soiled with blood and body fluids, as alcohol rubs do not clean physical debris. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the correct first step when removing (doffing) personal protective equipment?
explanation: Gloves are typically the most contaminated item of PPE and must be removed first during the doffing process. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following statements about medical gloves is correct?

options.A: Gloves can be washed with soap and water and reused for multiple patients
options.B: Gloves replace the need for hand hygiene after patient care
options.C: Gloves must be changed between patients and disposed of properly
options.D: Gloves are only required during surgical operations

explanation: Gloves must be changed between different patients and discarded appropriately to prevent cross-contamination, and they never replace hand hygiene. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of maintaining aseptic technique during invasive procedures?

options.A: To speed up the healing time of surgical incisions
options.B: To keep objects and areas as free from microorganisms as possible
options.C: To eliminate the need for administering systemic antibiotics
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of hospital supplies

explanation: Aseptic technique is specifically designed to keep items and sterile fields as free from microorganisms as possible to prevent infection. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h7)

question: How should an indwelling urinary catheter collection bag be positioned to prevent CAUTIs?

options.A: Above the level of the patient's bladder
options.B: Directly on the patient's bed sheets
options.C: Below the level of the bladder at all times
options.D: Hanging from the IV pole at head height

explanation: The catheter bag must always remain below the level of the bladder to prevent urine from flowing backward into the bladder and causing an infection. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h7)

question: Where must used needles and scalpel blades be disposed of immediately after use?
explanation: Sharps must always be discarded directly into puncture-resistant safety boxes to prevent needlestick injuries and accidental exposure. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h8)

question: What is the primary function of disinfecting high-touch hospital surfaces?

options.A: To remove dust and improve room appearance
options.B: To eliminate persistent reservoirs of pathogenic microorganisms
options.C: To keep the room smelling fresh for incoming patients
options.D: To reduce the humidity levels inside the clinical ward

explanation: Regular disinfection of high-touch surfaces eliminates microbial reservoirs that could otherwise transmit infections to patients and staff. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h8)

question: Why are bedside nurses ideally positioned to conduct infection surveillance?

options.A: They have advanced degrees in hospital administration
options.B: They spend the most continuous time at the patient's bedside
options.C: They are solely responsible for purchasing hospital disinfectants
options.D: They work exclusively in hospital microbiology laboratories

explanation: Bedside nurses spend the most continuous time observing patients, making them uniquely qualified to detect early signs of infection and unusual clinical trends. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h9)

question: What action should a nurse take immediately after experiencing an occupational needlestick injury?

options.A: Hide the incident so colleagues do not worry
options.B: Report the exposure promptly to ensure proper post-exposure management
options.C: Wait until the end of the month to mention it during evaluation
options.D: Take a self-prescribed dose of broad-spectrum antibiotics

explanation: Prompt reporting of occupational exposures ensures that the healthcare worker receives immediate post-exposure prophylaxis and appropriate medical follow-up. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h9)
